- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially after sharp spikes or volatility; model tends to peak too early and then decay too slowly.
- Underestimate during periods of sustained high prices; model fails to capture mean reversion or long-term trend continuation.
- Overshoot after initial spikes; model reacts too aggressively to short-term volatility, leading to overcorrection downward.
- Lag in response to true price drops; model often misses sudden declines, especially when preceded by high volatility.
- Overconfident in short-term forecasts; model shows excessive smoothing or inertia, failing to adjust to rapid changes.
- Underestimate true volatility in low-price regimes; model assumes stability when actual price swings are more pronounced.
- Model exhibits bias toward mid-range values; fails to capture extreme outliers, especially in the tails of the distribution.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts tend to be overly optimistic in the first 5–7 days, then gradually converge — model should adjust downward early if recent prices are trending up.
